anomaly_def.Name: Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located inside the buffer manager, where sessions stall while contending for shared buffer-cache pages, page pins, page-content locks, lightweight synchronization primitives, latches, in-flight I/O slots, or dirty-page flush slots. It sits below transaction-level row and table locks and is distinct from raw memory-size problems because the failure mode is page-level access serialization rather than overall memory exhaustion. Observable phenomena: elevated buffer-busy and page-latch wait events in engine wait-event views, prolonged latch acquisition reported by performance-tracing facilities, CPU spinning without throughput gain, and latency spikes concentrated on hot index root pages, sequence-like pages, or counter rows. Possible contributing factors: hot pages repeatedly accessed by many concurrent sessions, an undersized buffer pool that forces constant page churn, slow storage prolonging dirty-page flush cycles, aggressive checkpoint or background-writer settings, cleanup or bulk-load activity monopolizing buffer I/O, monotonic insert patterns concentrating writes on a single page, and inappropriate latch or spin-loop configuration in highly parallel workloads.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle, but not within an open transaction, for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle and not inside an open transaction longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; the documentation warns about using this with connection pools or middleware.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
